run_summary: Run 99. Selected NEX-099 by dependency readiness, not pattern continuation: the checkpoint closed the paging family at NEX-098 and said to pick the next dependency-ready task. Auditing the tenant-access seam found the demo identity provider as an uncounted fifth identity path -- NEX-006 covered three human paths, NEX-017 added agent tokens as a fourth, and the demo provider checked only is_active. A suspended or deprovisioned membership therefore still authenticated in development, which is the same offboarding gap the earlier slices closed everywhere else. Fixed by routing the demo provider through ensure_tenant_access, corrected the docstring to five paths, added 6 tests (2 positive controls, 4 refusals), and proved the guard load-bearing by reverting the one source file (exactly 4 red, controls green). The subtler finding: two existing organization tests were green ONLY because of this defect -- they asserted a 404 for a caller who had lost their only membership, which passed only because the demo path let that caller stay authenticated past the boundary. Rather than change their expected status (which would have quietly weakened what they assert), each now gives Bob a second active membership so the original assertions test org invisibility and terminal offboarding as named.
